title: Bounty Hunting - Marshal Canton Lore & Dialogue
blurb: Who Marshal Canton is, where to find him, the clues about the man in the machine, and every line he says, laid out as the conversation menus you see in game.

sections.title: Who Is Marshal Canton?
sections.html:
Marshal Canton is the bounty giver for Skyline Valley. He stands at The Trading Post by the Bounty Board and hands out Grunt Hunts and Head Hunts.

{img:canton-trading-post.avif}

He is a robot in a cowboy hat with a glass dome on top, and he introduces himself as "Frank Canton, United States Marshal". He says he was first appointed as a Marshal in Oklahoma in 1894, and that "this whole robot business came later".

He talks like an old Western lawman: outlaws, rustlers, desperadoes, the Law with a capital L. He no longer has a body that can handle rough ground ("this goddarned drive motor"), so he farms the gunslinging out to bounty hunters.

There's no pay from him, because "the governor ain't exactly been filling the kitty lately". You keep whatever you loot. Head Hunt contracts, though, cost a 5,000-cap "charitable donation".

Is he really Frank Canton?

Push him on his past and the act cracks. With Intelligence 12+ you can tell him the real Frank Canton died in the 1920s. Ask him to explain and he breaks down mid-sentence: "Oh, God, what've they done to me? Where am I? What happened to the spa?" Then he snaps back and refuses to talk about it.

{img:canton-personal-questions.avif}

The Scan 14: Josiah Harrison holotape from A Matter of Matter (Rapidan Camp) has Canton's voice in it. Iggy Stolz tells him: "You're not even really you, just a miscalibration of a has-been actor." Canton answers "Actor? What kind of..." and goes into the same pained "Where am I? Why can't I see anything?" breakdown.

Put together, it looks like the brain in the robot was scanned from someone who played Frank Canton, and the personality took over. The tape's title names Josiah Harrison. He never says this in one line, so treat it as a reading of the clues rather than a stated fact.

Little details

  • He hums "Camptown Races" while idle, keeps losing his hat ("Got a powerful need for some more glue") and can't remember where he got it.
  • "Nothing like fresh air. Be real nice if I could still smell it."
  • He greets you differently if you're a ghoul the first time you meet.
  • He has worked "with every cattle baron, sheriff's office, Pinkerton, and governor from Wyoming to Texas".

sections.title: Where to Find Him
sections.html: The Trading Post, Skyline Valley, next to the Bounty Board.

sections.title: Quests & Activities
sections.html:
• Skyline Valley Grunt Hunts and Head Hunts. If you've already finished a Burning Springs Grunt Hunt you can skip most of his pitch with "You mean bounty hunting."
  • Chasing A Lead. Bring him the strange coded message and he decodes it, explaining that outlaws hide messages in slang and code.
  • A Matter of Matter. His voice is on the Scan 14 holotape (see Lore Documents).

sections.title: Buying a Wanted Poster
sections.html:
He sells Skyline Valley Wanted Posters through his conversation, not a shop menu. The full steps with pictures are on the Skyline Valley Head Hunt Guide.

  1. First time: "You must have something more challenging than these bounties." → "So, tell me about these “desperadoes”." → "I'll take one of these premium contracts." → "[5,000 Caps] Here's your “donation.”"
  2. After that: "I'm looking for a premium contract." → "[5,000 Caps] Here's your “donation.”"

You need 5,000 caps on you, and he won't sell one while you already carry a Skyline Valley Wanted Poster.

docs.text:
Iggy Stolz: He said he never had a son. He wrote the songs from his own perspective.
Marshal Canton: Who gives a damn? No one should be writing ditties about anything other than their horse, the open prairie, or gunning down desperadoes.
Iggy Stolz: It's, uh... It's just so similar to our own situation. I'm just surprised he still...
Marshal Canton: So, what of it? That why you get up in the morning? To live for his approval?
Marshal Canton: You need to be more than what he thinks of you, boy. A man defines himself, nobody else.
Iggy Stolz: I dunno...
Marshal Canton: What is left of you when he's gone? If it's anything less than all of you, it's a damn fool's errand to live like that.
Iggy Stolz: Okay. I guess so.
Marshal Canton: If you want to wallow in your failure like some muck-happy pig, you do that on your time and don't involve me.
Marshal Canton: Leave the sorrows of the past in the past. It's no way to live, carrying them around, haunting you like ghosts.
Iggy Stolz: Oh, sure, I...
Iggy Stolz: Why am I even talking to you? You're not even really you, just a miscalibration of a has-been actor.
Marshal Canton: Actor? What kind of...
Marshal Canton: *Pained noises*
Marshal Canton: Where am I? Why can't I see anything? It hurts...
Marshal Canton: *Pained noises*
Marshal Canton: Come on, now, those outlaws won't be far. The time for fireside chats is over. Grab your iron and we'll...

items.prompt: Problem? Solution? What are you talking about?
lines: I'm talking about the Law, you hopped-up prairie dog.
Name's Frank Canton, U.S. Marshal, and for my sins I'm what passes for the Law in these parts.

items.prompt: I don't mean you any harm, if that's what you're asking.
lines: Then we'll get on just fine, you and I.
Frank Canton, United States Marshal, at your service. Insofar as this here savage territory has Law, I'm it.

items.prompt: Problem. Definitely a problem.
lines: *Spit out*
Well, we'll just see about that. I've got ways of turning the one into the other.
I am United States Marshal Frank Canton, and as far as you're concerned, I am the Law here.

items.prompt: Whoa, a robot with a hat!
lines: Oh, I see. A saphead. Could go either way, then.
I'm Frank Canton, U.S. Marshal for these parts. Far as you're concerned, I'm the Law around here, and don't you forget it.
With the introductory jolly out of the way, let's get to business.
Bloodthirsty rustlers and outlaws of every sort think they've got free reign without any Law to constrain them.
This here territory has gone far too long without someone bringing the hammer of righteous justice down upon them! And I mean to correct that.
Fortunately for you, I'm short a posse or two, so I'm looking to farm out the gunslinging.

items.prompt: Farm out the gunslinging?
lines: Bounty hunting, you clodhopper. *Sigh* I've got a list of miscreants long as the Mississippi, and no desire to man a pokey.
I'd love to shoot the bastards myself if it weren't for this goddarned drive motor. Just can't handle the rough terrain like I used to good.
conds: Only until: asked about gunslinging

items.prompt: Oh, you mean bounty hunting. No need to sell me. I'm in.
lines: *Laugh* By Jiminy, I thought you had it in you!
See that pile of paper? Every sheet's another name. Grab one and introduce yourself.
Of course, if you're thinking of bigger fish, we might be able to make a deal.
conds: Only after you have completed Burning Springs: Grunt Hunt

items.prompt: How's this bounty hunting work, then?
lines: Oh, nothing too complicated. Reckon even a Yank could figure it out.
See, the Lawman and the outlaw alike live by the gun. Seeing to it the right one also dies by it... *Laugh* That's the heart of the matter.
You get a target. You send them to the bone orchard with some lead to keep them company on the journey
Then, job done, hit the saloon, bend an elbow, and do some twelve-ounce curls.
conds: Only after: asked about gunslinging

items.prompt: You mean bounty hunting.
lines: Ding, ding, ding! Right on the mark. Not a greenhorn in the business, then.
There's plenty of work for an experienced hand.
conds: Only after you have completed Burning Springs: Grunt Hunt

items.prompt: You're a robot and the U.S.A. is gone. What are you talking about?
lines: My infirmities and the state of this fair land don't change the facts of the matter.
Outlaws get put down. That's what they're made for! Been that way all my born days, and I mean to see to it that it keeps being that way.

items.prompt: A robot Marshal? I have so many questions.
lines: Luckily for you, I weren't going anywhere today.

items.prompt: All right, give me a bounty.
I don't work for free.
lines: Nor should you.
Ahem! Times being what they are, though, money ain't in the picture. Not directly, anyway. The governor ain't exactly been filling the kitty lately.
Still, greed is the defining trait of the outlaw, and fear is his weapon.
So, how's about you and I learn these scoundrels the real meaning of fear, huh? And if you happen to relieve them of some of their ill-gotten gains, well...
I ain't the taxman.

items.prompt: I'm not a killer for hire.
lines: Someone once told me, "Every sunrise is a chance to be a different person."
Mind you, that someone was a cattle rustler, and he said it staring down the barrel of my big iron here.
Didn't change what came next, but it doesn't mean he weren't right, neither.

items.prompt: I've got some other questions first.
Time for me to get to work.
lines: I envy you. *Sigh* Well, go on then. Git! Put one between their eyes for me, while you're at it.

items.prompt: And you just trust that I'll get the job done?
lines: Trust don't enter into it, partner.
Either your target ends up taking a dirt nap, in which case I'll hear about it and don't you worry about how, or you blow it.
In which case, I'll probably hear about that too, and send somebody better to finish the job.

items.prompt: So there's no money in this at all?
lines: I gather you're from outside the territory, so you might not've noticed this ain't exactly the big city.
I put these contracts out because every Jack in them is barely above a snake and in dire need of putting down.
Turn out their pockets and melt down their fillings, for all I care, if profit's what you need.

items.prompt: You're just putting out hits on people, all on your own?
lines: Until some territorial governor or other official comes down the pike and tells me different, I'm still the Law and I'll keep doing what needs doing.
I've worked with every cattle baron, sheriff's office, Pinkerton, and governor from Wyoming to Texas, and the job's always the same.
Somebody draws the short straw, and somebody like me picks up iron to put an end to their miserable tale.
conds: Only after: asked about money

items.prompt: You mentioned something about "bigger fish"?
lines: *Laugh* Regular threats to life and limb not enough for you, eh?
See, those curs in that there stack of contracts are villains to a one, but there's other outlaws what make them look like altar boys.
Desperadoes what've filled more graves than you've had hot meals. Scum of the earth, no two ways about it.
I keep track of them, of course, but I don't put out a contract on them for just anyone.

items.prompt: How'd a robot get to be a U.S. Marshal?
lines: Same way as any other Marshal, I reckon. I just weren't always a robot, of course.
It was back in 1894, when I was first appointed out in Oklahoma. This ain't my first time wearing a badge, mind you.
This whole robot business came later.
conds: Only until: asked about robot

items.prompt: 1894? That's over two hundred years ago!
lines: Don't think my advanced years are going to stop me from stripping your hide, neither. Show some respect to your elders!
conds: Only after: asked about robot

items.prompt: But that's impossible. Robots wouldn't be invented for over a century.
lines: Now, look here, you whippersnapper, I... I...
There's a perfectly reasonable explanation.
conds: Only after: asked about robot

items.prompt: [INT 12+] Hang on, the real Frank Canton died in the 1920s. You can't possibly be him.
lines: Dead? Now, do I look dead to you? Can't be me, ha! What hogwash! I think I'd know if I weren't myself.
Don't you come lecturing me like some Ivy League windbag.
conds: Intelligence 12+

items.prompt: Okay, explain it to me, then.
lines: If it'll shut up all your goddarned chicken-clucking, I will!
You see, I... Well, the way it went was... It's been so long, the memory gets hazy... Maybe too much Whiskey...
I... I was... Eugh...
Oh, God, what've they done to me? Where am I? What happened to the spa?
I... *Pained groans*
I think we've jawed enough about this subject. You're putting me off my dang coffee.
conds: Only after: you've questioned who he really is
Only until: the breakdown scene

items.prompt: What the hell was that?
lines: What was what? Didn't I tell you I've had enough of your prying into my affairs? There's hunting to be done. Git!
conds: Only after: the breakdown scene

items.prompt: Let's talk about something else.
lines: Reckon that's for the best.

items.prompt: So, tell me about these "desperadoes".
lines: I ain't gonna surgarcoat it for you, kid. Folks who go after these fellas, well, they wind up dead themselves, mostly.
Which is, mostly, not my problem. It's not like the poor saps can come back and complain about it, anyways. I warned them, just as I'm warning you, now.
But these contracts are open. You having them ain't going to stop any other hunters joining in, and you might as well let them. More chance of surviving, I reckon.
As a consequence, these are strictly one at a time. Somebody's got one posted, go help or wait 'til they're dead.
Lastly and most importantly, the Law don't fund itself. You might not think it, but it takes a fair few caps to keep this operation running.
So, if you want one of these contracts, I regretfully require a charitable donation.
conds: Only until: asked about head hunts

items.prompt: I'll take one of these premium contracts.
lines: Why, you've got the fires of justice in you! No doubt about it.
Now, about that donation...
conds: Only after: asked about head hunts

items.prompt: You've talked me out of it.
lines: No shame in that, kid. No sense getting yourself killed.
Come find me again if you change your mind, though.

items.prompt: [5,000 Caps] Here's your "donation."
lines: Well, that's mighty fine of you. This'll keep the light of the Law on this blasted land. Metaphorically speaking, of course.
Now, take this here bounty notice. Nail it up on that board yonder, so anybody looking knows the contract's open.
Happy trails, hunter. Try and keep your head attached.
conds: Needs 5,000 caps

items.prompt: How big of a donation are we talking about?
lines: Regretfully, a mighty sum indeed. I take no pleasure in it, I assure you, but needs must when the Devil drives.
And there are so very many devils in the Wasteland.
conds: Only until: asked about cost

items.prompt: I'm not ready to make any donations right now.
lines: And there's no shame in that. Times are tough all over.

items.prompt: I'm here for another bounty.
lines: Perfection. Pile's right there; feel free to help yourself.
Keep your iron handy, and good luck.

items.prompt: You must have something more challenging than these bounties.
conds: Only if you have never completed Skyline Valley: Head Hunt
Only until: asked about head hunts

items.prompt: I'm looking for a premium contract.
lines: Well, let's see...
conds: Only after: asked about head hunts

items.prompt: I've actually got some other questions for you.

lines: Glad to see you so eager. We just need to discuss that charitable donation, of course.
conds: Only if you don't have a Skyline Valley Wanted Poster

lines: Now, I already told you once: One at a time. You've got a contract. Come back when they're cold, and then, we can talk.
conds: Only if you already have a Skyline Valley Wanted Poster

items.prompt: I found this strange message, and all I can make out is your name.
Any idea what this weird note is? It's got your name on it, but I can't make sense of anything else.
lines: My name, eh? Let me see that...
Aha! I can see why you'd be confused. This is written in code! Mostly, anyway. Outlaws can barely put two words on paper, in my experience.
What you've got here is a scrap of communication between criminals. They think they're real clever-like, hiding the message in slang and codes and such like this.
Fortunately for the Law, they ain't that clever. Once you've figured it out it's clear as day. Here, let me learn y'all how it works...
See? This is actually discussing a gang hideout. I can show you on your map. Right...here.
Couldn't ask for a better lead, if you were looking to take the fight to them.

items.prompt: Anything else you can tell me?
lines: Well, now that you understand the code they use, if you find more of this sort of thing you might could put the clues together to find yourself a bigger fish.
Personally, I'm content to whittle them down one by one, but I reckon some hunters prefer cutting the head off the rattlesnake.
I'll show you what to look for. Mind you, if you go hunting the big game, there's always a bigger predator out there. So, keep sharp.
Good hunting. Try not to end up in a wood box yourself.

items.prompt: So, why are you mentioned here?
lines: Because I am the Law, of course. I assume this miscreant you took this off of is probably somebody I've been on the trail of before, and they lived in fear of me.
Right of them to do so. It is natural. Just a shame I wasn't involved in their much-deserved end.
Still, it warms a Marshal's heart to know I'm ever-present in their tiny, criminal minds.
Metaphorically speaking, of course. I'm fusion-powered these days.

items.prompt: And I just go to this location and...what? Kill everybody?
lines: The big dog, at least, simple enough. In my experience, works every time. *Laugh* And the story always tells better when nobody's left to contradict you.
If you're feeling soft-hearted, I suppose you could try talking at them first and hope they're peaceable. See where that gets you. I knew a sheriff's deputy would tried that, once.
God rest his stupid soul.
Well, well, well. Aren't you a strange tumbleweed. Marshal Frank Canton, at your service, if you didn't know already. Something I can do for you?
conds: Only until: you've met

lines: Back again for a bounty, or you got something else on your mind?
conds: Before the lead has been decoded
Only after: you've met

lines: Well, well. The mighty hunter returns!
If it ain't the long arm of my claw!
Pray tell, what can this old Marshal do for you?
If that ain't a sight for sore circuits. I recognize this here tumbleweed. Something an old Law Dog can do for you?
No time to waste, friend. Get the contract, and get to killing.
conds: Only after: you've heard how bounty hunting works
Only after: you've asked for a bounty

lines: So, are you interested in taking a bounty, or are you too busy wasting breath?
conds: Only after: you've heard how bounty hunting works
Only until: you've asked for a bounty

lines: Mayhaps now you're done fooling around?
conds: Only until: you've heard how bounty hunting works
Only after: the introduction is done

lines: What've we got here, then? You part of the problem, or part of the solution?
conds: Only until: you've met
If you are not a ghoul

lines: Hrm. You look like trouble to me, but looks ain't everything. What's it going to be, then? Problem, or solution?
conds: Only until: you've met
If you are a ghoul

lines: You again, eh? What've you got today? Another problem? Or are you looking to be part of the solution?
conds: Only after: you've met

lines: Howdy there.
Here for a bounty?
Keep it peaceable, partner.
No need for the big iron here.
I've got my eye on you.
Bit overdressed, aren't you?
Lawman for hire's still a lawman. *Laugh* I should know.
Take any trouble somewhere else, stranger.
Looking for work?
Well, now, look what the cat dragged in.
*Humming "Camptown Races"*
*Spit out* Outlaws... Ugh! Disgusting.
My, my, my! What a fine day for putting down rustlers.
Nothing like fresh air. Be real nice if I could still smell it.
Always more killing needs doing. Never a shortage of crime.
Got a powerful need for some more glue...can't be losing my hat again. Where did I even get this thing?
I reckon that storm can't be good. Makes for a mighty nice sky, though.
Aw, consarn it! Where'd I leave those bullets?
